To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the BFKL evolution equation can be modified to account for gluon fusion, that this modified equation predicts a strong gluon shadowing and gluon disappearance, and that this effect can be understood as a chaotic behavior of the modified BFKL evolution.
the BFKL gluon fusion is a non-trivial process and that its corrections to the equation are important.

(i) the gluon fusion corrections lead to a strong suppression of the gluon distribution at low x; (ii) this suppression can be interpreted as the gluon disappearance; (iii) the new BFKL equation with gluon fusion corrections predicts a chaotic solution; (iv) a possible chaotic solution can lead to the gluon density saturation.

the following questions:   1.
the study of the gluon distribution at very small x, which is of great importance for understanding the high energy hadron collisions.
the study of the BFKL evolution of partons in the proton.

the new equation predicts a stronger saturation, which may lead to the gluon extinction at small x.
the gluon distribution is not as small as the BFKL predicts at small x, but it may be even larger.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the gluon fusion corrections to the BFKK equation lead to a new perspective on the gluon distribution at very small x.
the BFKL evolution is not necessarily the only way to describe the gluon distribution at high energies.
